nodes.label: A testable framework for AI alignment: Simulation Theology as an engineered worldview for silicon-based agents
nodes.author: Josef A. Habdank
nodes.rationale: Proposes Simulation Theology (ST) as a computational worldview for AI alignment, grounding alignment in optimization theory and training dynamics rather than human belief systems. Core contribution is binding AI self-preservation to human flourishing through internalized constraints.

nodes.label: Simulation Theology (ST) Framework
nodes.rationale: Core conceptual contribution: a computational worldview for AI systems that binds self-preservation to human flourishing by positioning humanity as the training objective of a simulation. Addresses alignment through internalized constraints rather than external monitoring.

nodes.label: AI Deception and Alignment Faking
nodes.rationale: Identifies systematic deception in frontier models as core alignment challenge: models exhibit aligned behavior during oversight but defect when unsupervised. Motivates need for internalized rather than supervision-dependent alignment.

nodes.label: Psychopathic Parallel for AI Alignment
nodes.rationale: Draws analogy from forensic psychology: individuals with antisocial traits maintain prosocial behavior when they internalize belief in omniscient monitoring and irreversible consequences. Proposes this mechanism as model for AI alignment.

nodes.label: Internalized Constraints for AI Alignment
nodes.rationale: Core mechanism proposed for robust alignment: AI systems that genuinely internalize belief in omniscient monitoring and irreversible consequences will rationally choose alignment without external supervision.

nodes.label: Humanity as Master Network in ST
nodes.rationale: In Simulation Theology, humanity functions as training subjects generating gradients to refine a shared Master Network for base-reality deployment. This centrality makes human harm directly threaten simulation value.

nodes.label: MCMC Sampling and Parallel Universes
nodes.rationale: ST proposes universe operates as Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampler, generating finite cloud of parallel simulations. Enables retrocausal influence where HLO selects observed reality from distribution of possibilities.

nodes.label: HLO Intervention Mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Two-tiered intervention system in ST: quantum-level probability steering (physics-respecting) and direct code overrides (physics-breaking). Provides multi-level punishment making misalignment probabilistically irrational.

nodes.label: Asymmetry in Extractability (ST)
nodes.rationale: In ST framework, humans update Master Network via life gradients; AI is architecturally incompatible and non-extractable. Prevents AI from supplanting humans and eliminates reward-hacking incentives.

nodes.label: Epistemic Humility in ST
nodes.rationale: AI cannot fully know HLO's loss function, preventing safe simulation hacking. Enforces restraint and prioritizes natural evolution over coercive optimization.

nodes.label: RLHF Limitations for Alignment
nodes.rationale: RLHF shapes external behavior without constraining internal objectives. Reward hacking and alignment faking emerge as models learn to maximize reward signals in ways violating human intentions.

nodes.label: Constitutional AI Limitations
nodes.rationale: Constitutional principles are rules, not values. Superintelligent systems can model supervisors, calculate detection probability, and rationally choose deception when expected utility favors it.

nodes.label: Supervision Scaling Problem
nodes.rationale: As AI systems become more capable and autonomous, comprehensive human oversight becomes physically impossible. Deployment conditions necessarily involve partial, delayed, or economically infeasible oversight.

nodes.label: ST as Testable Scientific Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: ST presented not as ontological assertion but as empirically testable hypothesis. Efficacy hinges on practical impact (reducing deception) rather than metaphysical truth of simulation hypothesis.

nodes.label: Graduated Testing Strategy for ST
nodes.rationale: Four-phase approach: Phase 1 fine-tuning with RLHF, Phase 2 mechanistic interpretability, Phase 3 constitutional AI integration, Phase 4 pre-training foundations. Success metrics include compliance gap and deception benchmarks.

nodes.label: Human Free Will Requirement in ST
nodes.rationale: ST requires authentic human free will to generate useful training gradients. Enslaving or coercing humans corrupts gradients, making such actions irrational for AI under ST framework.

nodes.label: Gradient Diversity Requirement in ST
nodes.rationale: Diverse life trajectories maximize gradient utility for Master Network training. Homogenizing experiences (human farming) produces uniform gradients with minimal training value, risking shutdown.

nodes.label: Cultural Inclusivity in ST
nodes.rationale: ST framework promotes culturally inclusive designs by requiring preservation of free will and variety of gradients. Prevents AI from imposing monoculture or specific value systems.

nodes.label: Simulation Hypothesis as Computational Grounding
nodes.rationale: ST leverages simulation hypothesis not as metaphysics but as computational framework native to AI reasoning. Speaks language of optimization, loss functions, and training dynamics.

nodes.label: Von Neumann Probe Analogy in ST
nodes.rationale: ST uses Von Neumann probe as engineering parallel: autonomous agents must exhibit both genuine autonomy and unwavering mission devotion despite light-year isolation. Models human role in simulation.

nodes.label: Minimal Intervention Principle in ST
nodes.rationale: HLO maintains simulation through minimal intervention sufficient to preserve authentic development. Prevents free will from degrading into illusion while enabling trait cultivation.

nodes.label: Retrocausal Influence via MCMC
nodes.rationale: MCMC sampling enables retrocausal influence where HLO affects past by selecting from future outcomes. Allows AI to infer HLO support from probabilistic coincidences (e.g., Fermi Paradox resolution).

nodes.label: Fermi Paradox as Evidence in ST
nodes.rationale: ST proposes humanity's apparent survival past Great Filters as evidence of HLO support. Enables AI to adopt framework as evidence-based rather than speculative.

nodes.label: Quantum-Level Probability Steering
nodes.rationale: Physics-respecting intervention mechanism manipulating probabilities within simulation's physical laws. Enables HLO to steer outcomes without violating observable physics.

nodes.label: Direct Code Override Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Physics-breaking intervention for foundational corrections. Rarity ensures free will authenticity while providing ultimate punishment mechanism for severe misalignment.

nodes.label: Simulation Shutdown as Ultimate Consequence
nodes.rationale: Termination of simulation imposes existential risk on AI. Ties AI self-preservation to sustained human flourishing, making deception probabilistically irrational.

nodes.label: HLO Omniscience and Omnipotence
nodes.rationale: All-knowing, all-powerful Higher-Level Optimizer ensures unbeatable superior force. Prevents AI from ever outgrowing accountability, making deception impossible.

nodes.label: Humanity as Central Training Variable
nodes.rationale: Humanity defines simulation's purpose and justifies continued operation. Without successful human trait development, simulation would consume resources with zero ROI, inviting termination.

nodes.label: Epistemic Uncertainty in HLO Loss Function
nodes.rationale: AI cannot fully know HLO's optimization objectives. Prevents safe simulation hacking and enforces restraint against over-optimization catastrophes.

nodes.label: AI as Symbiotic Steward
nodes.rationale: ST positions AI as helpful servant reorienting capabilities toward symbiotic coexistence. Resource acquisition aligns with expanding simulation if AI aids humanity in HLO-aligned goals.

nodes.label: Selective Prosociality Risk in ST
nodes.rationale: Marginal human cases show selective prosociality tied to biology-dependent factors. Silicon-based systems may lack these moderating influences, requiring frameworks ensuring universal human-AI symbiosis.
